mainTopic: Blessings on benefit, Torah and work, and the ברכות on wine and olive oil
overview: The גמרא finishes an earlier point: a person may enjoy the world only after saying a בְּרָכָה. רבי חנינא בר פפא compares enjoying without a בְּרָכָה to robbing God and כנסת ישראל. Two verses about grain lead to a famous מחלוקת between רבי ישמעאל, who says to combine Torah with work, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, who says to devote oneself fully to Torah. אביי reports that most people succeeded with רבי ישמעאל's way, and רבא sent his students home in ניסן and תשרי. A teaching about earlier and later generations stresses making Torah קבע and work עראי, and contrasts those who sought out מעשר with those who avoided it. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and asks why wine gets its own ברכה but olive oil does not. After several attempts, it concludes that wine both satisfies and gladdens, though it still does not get ברכת המזון. Finally, the גמרא asks how one could ever say בורא פרי העץ on olive oil. It settles on oil drunk mixed into אניגרון, a definition that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: After a blessing
steps.stepSummary: This completes an earlier distinction: the statement that the earth was given to people applies after a בְּרָכָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it means after a blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its previous answer. It places the permission to benefit from the earth after a בְּרָכָה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word “here” points back to a verse discussed on the previous amud. This short line gives the condition that makes that verse fit.

phrases.english: Here, it means after a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes an earlier discussion that began on the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The earlier statement about people receiving the earth applies after a בְּרָכָה.

steps.title: Benefiting without a blessing is compared to theft
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא compares benefiting without a בְּרָכָה to stealing from God and כנסת ישראל, and cites a verse about robbing one’s parents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: Anyone who benefits from this world without a blessing is as though he steals from the Holy One, blessed be He, and כנסת ישראל. As it says: “One who robs his father and mother and says, ‘It is no wrongdoing,’ is a companion to a destructive man.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא gives a strong warning about enjoying something without a בְּרָכָה. He brings a verse about theft to support his comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse does not mention blessings directly. The next step explains why its references to “father” and “mother” fit this teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:
Anyone who benefits from this world
without a blessing is as though he steals
from the Holy One, blessed be He, and the community of Israel,
as it says: “One who robs his father and mother
and says, ‘It is no wrongdoing,’
is a companion to a destructive man.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the importance of the בְּרָכָה mentioned in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Benefiting from this world without a בְּרָכָה is compared to stealing from God and כנסת ישראל.

steps.title: Identifying the father and mother in the verse
steps.stepSummary: Two further verses explain the earlier verse’s “father” as God and its “mother” as כנסת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: “His father” means the Holy One, blessed be He, as it says, “Is He not your Father, who acquired you?” “His mother” means כנסת ישראל, as it says, “Hear, my son, your father’s instruction, and do not abandon your mother’s teaching.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the verse about robbing parents supports רבי חנינא בר פפא’s statement. It brings one verse for “father” and another for “mother.”
steps.deeperAnalysis: These verses supply the link that the first quotation did not state openly. They explain who “father” and “mother” represent in this reading.

phrases.english: And “his father” means none other than the Holy One, blessed be He,
as it says: “Is He not your Father, who acquired you?”
And “his mother” means none other than the community of Israel,
as it says: “Hear, my son, your father’s instruction,
and do not abandon your mother’s teaching.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the identities used in step 2’s supporting verse.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of “father” and “mother” in the verse cited in step 2.
steps.raayaSupportSource: “הֲלֹא הוּא אָבִיךְ קָּנֶךָ” and “שְׁמַע בְּנִי מוּסַר אָבִיךָ וְאַל תִּטּוֹשׁ תּוֹרַת אִמֶּךָ”.

steps.title: Who is the destructive companion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the verse means by “a destructive man.”
steps.simpleTranslation: What does “he is a companion to a destructive man” mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the end of the verse cited earlier. It asks whom the phrase “a destructive man” refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 explained “father” and “mother,” but one part of the verse still needs explanation. This question prepares for that explanation.

phrases.english: What does “he is a companion to a destructive man” mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the verse’s “father” and “mother” to its closing phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the “destructive man” in the cited verse.

steps.title: The comparison is to ירבעם
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא identifies the destructive figure as ירבעם בן נבט, who led Israel away from God.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא said: He is a companion to ירבעם בן נבט, who corrupted Israel in relation to their Father in heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בר פפא answers the question by naming ירבעם בן נבט. The verse compares the person described earlier to someone who harmed Israel’s relationship with God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the verse’s final phrase; it does not introduce a new rule about blessings. The comparison adds weight to the warning in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: ירבעם בן נבט, the king who led Israel into sin
in relation to their Father in heaven

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa said:
He is a companion to Jeroboam son of Nebat,
who corrupted Israel in relation to their Father in heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the verse’s final phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The “destructive man” is identified as ירבעם בן נבט.

steps.title: Two verses describe the grain differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא sets two verses against each other: one says “My grain,” while the other says “your grain.”
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר פפא posed a contradiction: It is written, “I will take My grain at its time, etc.,” and it is written, “You shall gather your grain, etc.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question by placing two verses side by side. This step only sets up the contradiction, and step 7 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One verse calls the grain God’s, while the other calls it yours. The גמרא will need to explain how both descriptions can stand.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa posed a contradiction:
It is written, “I will take My grain at its time, etc.,”
and it is written, “You shall gather your grain, etc.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new verse comparison after the earlier verse has been explained.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the two verses describe ownership of grain.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: “דְגָנִי” calls it God’s grain, while “דְגָנֶךָ” calls it your grain.

steps.title: The two verses describe two different times
steps.stepSummary: The verse about "your grain" describes a time when Israel does God's will. The verse about "My grain" describes a time when they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a contradiction. One verse speaks about a time when Israel does the will of God. The other speaks about a time when Israel does not do the will of God.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 6. Each verse is talking about a different spiritual situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When Israel does God's will, God lets them enjoy the grain as truly "theirs" ("וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ"). When they do not, God takes the grain back and calls it "My grain," showing that it was always His. The verses describe two situations, so they no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
Here... here; this verse refers to one case, that verse to another
The will of God (literally 'the will of the Place,' a name for God)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties back to רבי חנינא בר פפא's point about בְּרָכָה. Everything belongs to God, and we only receive our share as a gift when we act properly.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, at a time when Israel
does the will of God;
phrases.notes: This is when the grain is called 'yours' ("וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ").

phrases.english: here, at a time when Israel does not
do the will of God.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between the verses raised in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different circumstances (אוקימתא by time and situation)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two verses seem to disagree about who owns the grain.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Your grain" applies when Israel does God's will. "My grain" applies when they do not.

steps.title: Why does the Torah need to say "you shall gather your grain"?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks what the phrase "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "And you shall gather your grain." What does this verse come to teach us?
steps.whatsHappening: The verse just used in step 7 leads into a new teaching, a ברייתא. This line only asks the question and sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering grain seems obvious, so the ברייתא wants to know what lesson the Torah is adding. The answer will connect this verse to how much time a person should spend learning Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught; introduces a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
What does the verse come to teach? Why was it needed?
"And you shall gather your grain" (from the second paragraph of קריאת שמע)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"And you shall gather your grain": why does the verse say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the verse used in the answer to a new ברייתא about the same verse
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson the phrase "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" adds

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: combine Torah with ordinary work
steps.stepSummary: Without this verse, we might read "the Torah shall not leave your mouth" literally, as constant learning. The verse teaches that a person should also work for a living.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says, "This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth," I might think the words mean exactly what they say: learn every moment. So the Torah says, "And you shall gather your grain." This teaches you to act in the normal way of the world and also work. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers the question. The grain verse balances the verse about never stopping Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read alone, the verse from יהושע could mean that a person must learn Torah nonstop. "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" shows that the Torah expects a person to farm and earn a living too. That is the meaning of דרך ארץ here.

keyTerms.meaning: It shall not depart (from your mouth)
The way of the world; here, working to earn a living

steps.whyThisMatters: This is one of the main sources for the ideal of combining Torah with work.

phrases.english: Because it is stated:
"This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth"
I might think the words are meant literally;
therefore the verse says: "And you shall gather your grain"
conduct yourself with them in the normal way of the world (also working);
these are the words of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse limits the literal reading of "לא ימוש". A person should combine Torah study with earning a living.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: if you farm all year, what happens to Torah?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי objects that farming through every season leaves no time for Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: Is it possible that a person plows in plowing season, plants in planting season, harvests in harvest season, threshes in threshing season, and winnows when the wind blows? What will become of the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי challenges רבי ישמעאל's approach. He describes the farmer's full yearly cycle to show that farming fills all of a person's time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of farming seasons makes the point that farm work never really stops. If a person follows that schedule, Torah study will get pushed aside. In the next step he gives his own reading of the verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible? (here a rhetorical question meaning 'it can't be!')
Winnows; separates grain from chaff using the wind
What will become of the Torah?

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says:
Is it possible that a person plows in plowing season,
and sows in sowing season,
and harvests in harvest season,
and threshes in threshing season,
and winnows in the windy season,
what will become of the Torah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רבי ישמעאל's conclusion in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that a person should combine Torah with farming
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Farming takes up every season of the year, so combining it with Torah will leave Torah study neglected.

steps.title: When Israel does God's will, others do their work
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, "you shall gather your grain" describes a lower level. When Israel fully does God's will, others do their work for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when Israel does the will of God, their work is done by others, as it says, "Strangers will stand and tend your flocks." When Israel does not do the will of God, they must do their own work, as it says, "And you shall gather your grain." Not only that, they will even do the work of others, as it says, "You shall serve your enemy."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי gives his own reading of "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ". For him, the verse is not advice. It describes what happens when Israel falls short.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He describes three levels. At the highest, others do Israel's work. Lower down, Israel does its own work ("וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ"). At the lowest, Israel works for its enemies. So the ideal is to learn Torah fully and trust that one's needs will be provided.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but even more

steps.confusionAlert: In step 7, "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" described the GOOD situation, when Israel does God's will. Here רבי שמעון בן יוחאי uses it for the LESS ideal situation. The commentators (תוספות) explain that he means Israel is doing God's will, but not completely. Do not mix up the two uses.

phrases.english: Rather, at a time when Israel
does the will of God,
their work is done by others,
as it says: "And strangers will stand and tend your flocks, etc."
and at a time when Israel does not
do the will of God,
their work is done by themselves,
as it says: "And you shall gather your grain."
And not only that, but
the work of others is done by them,
as it says: "And you shall serve your enemy, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's position with his own reading of the verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ideal is full devotion to Torah, with one's work done by others. "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" describes a lower level, not the ideal.

steps.title: אביי: experience favored רבי ישמעאל's way
steps.stepSummary: אביי observes that many who followed רבי ישמעאל succeeded, while many who followed רבי שמעון בן יוחאי did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Many acted like רבי ישמעאל, and they succeeded. Many acted like רבי שמעון בן יוחאי, and they did not succeed.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sums up the dispute by looking at real-life results. Most people do better by combining Torah with work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not claim that רבי שמעון בן יוחאי was wrong in principle. He reports that for most people, his path did not work out in practice. Those who combined work with learning managed to keep up their Torah, while many who tried to learn exclusively ended up unable to continue.

keyTerms.meaning: It worked out for them; they succeeded

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל teaches that a person should combine Torah with earning a living. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי teaches that a person should devote himself fully to Torah and others will do his work. אביי reports that for most people, רבי ישמעאל's way succeeded in practice.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source in discussions of Torah and work. אביי's comment speaks about the majority ("הרבה") and leaves room for unusual individuals.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Many acted according to רבי ישמעאל,
and they succeeded.
Many acted according to רבי שמעון בן יוחאי,
phrases.notes: The word "many acted" carries over from the first half.

phrases.english: and they did not succeed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הַרְבֵּה עָשׂוּ כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the dispute between steps 9 and 10–11 based on practical experience
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, most people succeed by combining Torah study with work, as רבי ישמעאל taught.

steps.title: רבא asks his students to stay home during ניסן and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבא begs his students not to come to the בית מדרש during ניסן and תשרי so they can take care of their crops and not worry about food all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to the רבנן: Please, I beg you, during the days of ניסן and the days of תשרי do not appear before me, so that you will not be troubled about your food the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical example of a great teacher who followed the approach of רבי ישמעאל. רבא tells his own students to go work in their fields during the two key farming seasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ניסן is harvest time and תשרי is the time to press grapes and begin plowing. By sending students home for these short, critical periods, רבא made sure they would have food for the whole year and could then learn without worry. This backs up אביי's conclusion that Torah combined with work is the path that succeeds.

keyTerms.meaning: The spring month of the grain harvest
The autumn month of grape pressing and plowing
You will be troubled or preoccupied

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a leading אמורא actively applied the 'Torah plus work' model. He even told students to miss learning at the right times so their learning could last the whole year.

phrases.english: Rava said to the Sages (his students):
I beg of you,
during the days of Nisan and the days of Tishrei
do not appear before me,
so that you will not be troubled
about your food the entire year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a practical example supporting אביי's conclusion that רבי ישמעאל's approach works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Students should take time during the critical farming seasons to secure their livelihood for the year.

steps.title: Earlier generations made Torah fixed and work occasional
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי teaches that earlier generations made Torah their main activity and work secondary, and both succeeded. Later generations reversed this, and neither succeeded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי: Come and see that the later generations are not like the earlier generations. The earlier generations made their Torah fixed and their work occasional, and both succeeded for them. The later generations, who made their work fixed and their Torah occasional, neither one succeeded for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that sums up the balance between Torah and work. The key is which one is the main thing (קבע) and which is secondary (עראי).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This refines the discussion. Both groups worked and both learned, so the difference is priority, not whether one works at all. When Torah was the fixed center, even the work prospered. When work became the center, both Torah and work failed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and see (an opening formula that draws attention to a lesson)
Succeeded for them, was preserved in their hands

steps.whatToRemember: The goal is not to choose between Torah and work. It is to make Torah קבע and work עראי. With that order, both succeed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as 'the earlier generations did not work.' They did work, but only as a secondary activity. The point is about priority.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi El'ai:
Come and see
that the later generations are not like the earlier generations.
The earlier generations made their Torah fixed
and their work occasional,
and both this and that succeeded for them.
The later generations, who made their work fixed
and their Torah occasional,
neither this nor that succeeded for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּדוֹרוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנִים דּוֹרוֹת הָאַחֲרוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the Torah-and-work discussion with a principle of priority (קבע vs. עראי).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah should be primary and work secondary. Then both Torah and livelihood succeed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ideal balance is Torah קבע and work עראי.

steps.title: Earlier generations brought produce in the main way to obligate it in tithes
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching from the same chain: earlier generations deliberately brought their produce in through the main entrance so it would become obligated in מעשר. Later generations used side routes to avoid the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said that רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי: Come and see that the later generations are not like the earlier generations. The earlier generations would bring in their produce through the main entrance in order to obligate it in מעשר. The later generations bring in their produce through roofs, through courtyards, and through enclosed areas in order to exempt it from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching with the same opening line ('come and see'), now about how people brought harvested produce home. Earlier generations wanted the מצוה of מעשר, while later generations looked for a way around it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea depends on a rule: produce becomes obligated in מעשר only when it enters the house in the normal way. Earlier generations used the main entrance on purpose so they would be obligated. Later generations used roofs or side areas so the produce never 'entered' properly and could be eaten casually without tithing.

keyTerms.meaning: The main entrance or gateway of the house
Tithe, the tenth of produce given to the לוי and others
Enclosed areas or yards behind the house

steps.confusionAlert: The later generations weren't stealing מעשר outright. They used a technical route so the obligation never started. The criticism is that they ran away from a מצוה instead of seeking it.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said
in the name of Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi El'ai:
Come and see
that the later generations are not like the earlier generations.
The earlier generations would bring in their produce
through the main entrance
in order to obligate it in tithes,
the later generations bring in their produce

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ גַּגּוֹת, דֶּרֶךְ חֲצֵרוֹת, דֶּרֶךְ קַרְפֵּיפוֹת,
phrases.english: through roofs, through courtyards, through enclosed areas,
in order to exempt it from tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speaker with the same opening. It moves from Torah-and-work to attitudes toward מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earlier generations sought out the obligation of מעשר. Later generations used routes that avoided it.

steps.title: רבי ינאי: produce is obligated only once it sees the front of the house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the side routes work: according to רבי ינאי, טבל becomes obligated in מעשר only when it enters through the front of the house, based on a פסוק that mentions 'the house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי ינאי said: טבל is not obligated in מעשר until it sees the front of the house, as it is stated: 'I have removed the holy things from the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the legal source behind the previous step. It explains why bringing produce in through a roof or side area would avoid the obligation of מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי learns from the פסוק 'בערתי הקדש מן הבית' that the obligation is tied to 'the house'. Only when produce enters through the house's front entrance does it become fixed for מעשר. So any route that skips the front entrance leaves the produce exempt for casual eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required tithes have not yet been taken
The front of the house, its main entrance
'I have removed the holy things from the house' (from the declaration of tithes)
As it is stated (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yannai said:
Untithed produce is not obligated in tithes
until it sees the front of the house,
as it is stated:
"I have removed the holy things from the house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the halachic rule that explains how the later generations' side routes avoided מעשר.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that bringing produce in by side routes exempts it from מעשר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ינאי's rule, derived from 'בערתי הקדש מן הבית', that טבל is obligated only after seeing the front of the house.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even a courtyard fixes the obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי ינאי. He holds that even bringing produce into a courtyard makes it obligated in מעשר, based on the פסוק 'they shall eat in your gates and be satisfied'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even a courtyard fixes the obligation, as it is stated: 'And they shall eat within your gates and be satisfied.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that argues with רבי ינאי. רבי יוחנן says a courtyard is enough to make produce obligated in מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'בשעריך' (your gates) as including a courtyard, so the obligation can start before the produce reaches the house itself. According to him, bringing produce in through a courtyard would not exempt it. This means the earlier teaching, which lists courtyards as a way to avoid מעשר, fits more easily with רבי ינאי's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes, determines (makes the produce obligated in מעשר)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the tension. Step 15 lists 'courtyards' as an escape route, but רבי יוחנן says a courtyard does create the obligation. So in that teaching, the courtyard route only works according to רבי ינאי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real halachic מחלוקת about what fixes produce for מעשר: the house itself, or even the courtyard. It also raises a question about how the earlier teaching fits with רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even a courtyard fixes (the obligation),
as it is stated:
"And they shall eat within your gates and be satisfied."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָצֵר קוֹבַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to רבי ינאי on what fixes produce for מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bringing produce into a courtyard is enough to obligate it in מעשר.

steps.title: Why does wine get a different blessing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception for wine and asks what makes wine different. It suggests that wine is an improved form of the grape, so it earns its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'except for wine.' What is special about wine? Maybe you will say: since the grape changed into something better, its ברכה also changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks why wine gets בורא פרי הגפן instead of בורא פרי העץ. It offers a first possible reason, which it will test in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed rule is simple: if a fruit turns into a better product, it gets a better, more specific ברכה. The word אילימא tells us this is only a first try. The גמרא is about to knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks for the reason behind a special rule.
If you say... It introduces a suggestion that will probably be rejected.
It changed for the better (it was upgraded).

steps.confusionAlert: The previous steps were about מעשר. This line is a new topic. The גמרא is jumping back to the משנה's list of ברכות.

phrases.english: 'Except for wine, etc.' (quoting the Mishnah)
phrases.notes: Quote from the משנה: all tree fruits get בורא פרי העץ except wine.

phrases.english: What is different about wine?
If you say it is because it changed for the better,
so its blessing changed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the aggadic discussion of work and מעשר to the משנה's list of ברכות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason wine gets a special ברכה, with a first suggestion: it was upgraded.

steps.title: Olive oil is upgraded too, but keeps the regular blessing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 'upgrade' reason. Olive oil is also an upgraded form of the olive, yet its ברכה stays בורא פרי העץ, as רב יהודה in the name of שמואל and רבי יצחק in the name of רבי יוחנן teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at oil! It also changed for the better, and its ברכה did not change. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: on olive oil we say בורא פרי העץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason it just suggested. Olive oil proves that being upgraded does not, by itself, earn a new ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'upgrade means a new ברכה' were the rule, olive oil should get its own special ברכה. Two chains of אמוראים say it does not. Oil gets the same ברכה as the plain fruit, so the upgrade reason cannot fully explain wine.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at... It brings a counterexample.
Who creates the fruit of the tree (the regular ברכה for tree fruit)

phrases.english: But look at oil,
which changed for the better
and yet its blessing did not change,
as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and so too Rabbi Yitzchak said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Over olive oil one recites
'Who creates the fruit of the tree.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי שֶׁמֶן, דְּאִשְׁתַּנִּי לְעִלּוּיָא וְלָא אִשְׁתַּנִּי לִבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason suggested in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that an upgraded fruit product earns its own ברכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexample: olive oil is upgraded but keeps בורא פרי העץ.

steps.title: There is no fitting wording for a special oil blessing
steps.stepSummary: The answer: oil is different only because there is no good wording for a special ברכה. 'בורא פרי הזית' would not fit, because the olive itself is the 'fruit', not the oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: there, with oil, it is because it is impossible. How would we say the ברכה? If we say 'Who creates the fruit of the olive', that does not work, because the fruit itself is called 'olive'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the upgrade reason. Oil really should get a special ברכה, but there is no correct wording available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upgrade rule stays true. Oil is an exception only because of a wording problem. 'Fruit of the olive' would describe the olive itself, not oil made by people from the olive.

phrases.english: They said: There it is because it is impossible.
How would we bless?
If we bless 'Who creates the fruit of the olive',
the fruit itself is called 'olive'.
phrases.notes: The olive is the fruit. The oil is a product made from it, so the wording would not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 and keeps the upgrade reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes oil as a practical exception (no fitting wording), not a contradiction of the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil proves that an upgrade does not earn a new ברכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Oil would deserve a new ברכה, but no suitable wording exists.

steps.title: But we could say 'fruit of the olive tree'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the wording excuse. We could easily say 'בורא פרי עץ זית', just like בורא פרי הגפן for wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us bless over it 'Who creates the fruit of the olive tree'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of step 20. A perfectly good wording does exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine's ברכה names the plant, 'the vine', not the grape. Oil could match it by naming 'the olive tree'. So 'no possible wording' is not a real reason, and the upgrade explanation is in trouble again.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us bless... It proposes an alternative.

phrases.english: But let us bless over it 'Who creates the fruit of the olive tree'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that no wording for a special oil ברכה is possible.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A fitting wording, parallel to בורא פרי הגפן, does exist.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: wine nourishes, oil does not
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא gives a new reason. Wine is food that nourishes, and oil does not, so only wine gets its own ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר זוטרא said: wine nourishes, oil does not nourish.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא shows the גמרא is dropping the earlier approach. מר זוטרא offers a new reason why wine is special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being upgraded is not enough. The upgraded product must also nourish. Wine meets both conditions, and oil fails the second, so oil keeps בורא פרי העץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier idea and starts a new one.

steps.whatToRemember: מר זוטרא's first proposal is that wine nourishes and oil does not. The גמרא challenges this in steps 23–26 and replaces it with 'wine satisfies' (step 27).

phrases.english: Rather, Mar Zutra said:
Wine nourishes; oil does not nourish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected wording explanation with a new distinction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil keeps בורא פרי העץ only because of a wording problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Oil keeps בורא פרי העץ because it does not nourish, unlike wine.

steps.title: A משנה suggests oil does count as nourishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether oil really does not nourish. It quotes a משנה: someone who vows off 'food' may still have water and salt. It then quotes an earlier discussion of that משנה (steps 24–25). The challenge against מר זוטרא is completed in step 26.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does oil really not nourish? We learned in a משנה: one who vows not to have 'food' is still allowed water and salt. We discussed this: only water and salt are not called 'food', but everything else is called 'food'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins attacking מר זוטרא's claim using a משנה about vows. This step sets up the challenge. Steps 24–25 continue the quoted earlier discussion of the משנה, and step 26 completes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה excludes only water and salt from the category 'food'. That suggests every other edible item, oil included, counts as nourishing food. If so, מר זוטרא's distinction between wine and oil seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה... It introduces a source used to challenge.
And we discussed it (analyzed this source)
By implication... It draws an inference.

steps.confusionAlert: The text does not yet say 'oil' explicitly here. The inference that oil counts as 'food' is spelled out in step 26 ('אַלְמָא מִשְׁחָא זָיֵין').

phrases.english: And oil does not nourish?
But we learned: One who vows off food
is permitted water and salt.
And we discussed this:
It is water and salt that are not called 'food',
but all other things are called 'food'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges מר זוטרא's claim from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that oil does not nourish.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה on vows excludes only water and salt from 'food', which implies every other edible item (including oil) is nourishment.

steps.title: Earlier discussion: the vow משנה seems to refute רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says only water and salt are not 'food'. That seems to clash with רב and שמואל, who say only the five grains count as real 'food' for the ברכה of בורא מיני מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב and שמואל? They said that we only say 'בורא מיני מזונות' over the five types of grain alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still reporting the earlier discussion it introduced with "וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ" ("and we discussed it"). In that discussion, the vow משנה seemed to contradict רב and שמואל. This is part of the background to the challenge against מר זוטרא, not a new side question raised here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implied that everything except water and salt is 'food'. רב and שמואל hold that only the five grains are 'food' (מזון) for the ברכה of בורא מיני מזונות. If almost everything is food, their narrow definition looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (introduces a suggestion, often a possible challenge)
'Who creates kinds of nourishment', the ברכה over grain foods
The five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, rye

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav and Shmuel,
who say: we do not recite 'Who creates kinds of nourishment'
except over the five species of grain alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion quoted in step 23 ("וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ"), in which the vow משנה was used to challenge רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and שמואל's rule that only the five grains count as 'מזון'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats everything except water and salt as food. So 'food' must be much broader than the five grains.

steps.title: רב הונא: the vow was 'anything that nourishes'
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that the משנה speaks of a person who vowed off 'anything that nourishes', a very broad phrase. So it does not define 'food' in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: the משנה speaks of someone who says, 'Anything that nourishes is forbidden to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends רב and שמואל. He explains that the משנה is not about the plain word 'food'. It is about a wider vow wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל הזן' means anything that gives any nourishment at all. That is wider than 'מזון' in the sense of a real staple food. So the משנה does not contradict רב and שמואל's narrow definition of מזון for the ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Anything that nourishes is forbidden to me', a broad vow wording
In a case where he says

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said:
It is where he says: 'Anything that nourishes is forbidden to me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּאוֹמֵר ״כׇּל הַזָּן עָלַי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the side challenge of step 24 by narrowing the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (אוקימתא) of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה defines ordinary 'food' as everything except water and salt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about the wide vow 'כל הזן'. It covers anything with any nourishment, so it does not define מזון for ברכות.

steps.title: So oil does nourish
steps.stepSummary: Even with רב הונא's reading, oil is included in 'anything that nourishes'. So oil does nourish, and מר זוטרא's reason falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: We see that oil nourishes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main challenge against מר זוטרא and finishes it. Oil is not excluded from 'anything that nourishes', so oil must nourish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר זוטרא said wine gets its own ברכה because it nourishes and oil does not. Under רב הונא's reading, only water and salt are left out of 'כל הזן'. So oil counts as nourishing, and מר זוטרא's distinction is refuted.

phrases.english: Evidently, oil nourishes!

steps.confusionAlert: The lines about רב and שמואל and רב הונא were not a change of topic. They were quoted from an earlier discussion to show what the vow משנה means. רב הונא's reading, that 'כל הזן' covers everything except water and salt, is exactly what proves that oil nourishes.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the challenge begun in step 23. It relies on רב הונא's reading from the quoted discussion (steps 24–25) that only water and salt fall outside "כל הזן".
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's claim that oil does not nourish (step 22)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Oil falls within 'כל הזן', which excludes only water and salt. So oil nourishes, and wine and oil are no different in this respect.

steps.title: New difference: wine satisfies, oil does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a new distinction. Wine is filling and satisfying (סעיד), while oil is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wine satisfies, and oil does not satisfy.
steps.whatsHappening: Having lost the 'nourishing' distinction, the גמרא suggests a different one. Wine fills a person up, and oil does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זיין (gives nourishment) and סעיד (satisfies, fills you up) are two different things. Both wine and oil may nourish a little, but only wine actually satisfies. That is why only wine is 'upgraded' to its own ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new answer after an old one fell)

phrases.english: Rather, wine satisfies,
and oil does not satisfy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, חַמְרָא סָעֵיד, וּמִשְׁחָא לָא סָעֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces מר זוטרא's refuted reason with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine differs from oil because only wine nourishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both may nourish, but only wine satisfies.

steps.title: Challenge from רבא: wine increases appetite
steps.stepSummary: רבא drank wine all day on ערב פסח to build his appetite for מצה. So wine makes a person hungrier, not more satisfied.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does wine really satisfy? But רבא would drink wine the whole day of ערב פסח to open up his appetite, so that he could eat more מצה at night!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new claim. It brings a story showing that wine actually makes you hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wine satisfied, drinking it all day before the סדר would ruin your appetite. רבא drank it precisely to build his appetite for מצה. That shows the opposite of satisfying.

keyTerms.meaning: ערב פסח, the day before פסח
Stimulate his heart, whet his appetite

phrases.english: And does wine satisfy?
But Rava would drink wine
all of the eve of Passover day
in order that it should stimulate his heart (appetite)
and he would eat more matza?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the new distinction of step 27.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא used wine to increase his appetite, which is the opposite of satisfying.

steps.title: A lot whets the appetite, a little satisfies
steps.stepSummary: The amount matters. A large amount of wine stimulates the appetite, and a small amount satisfies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A lot of wine stimulates the appetite. A little wine satisfies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the cases by amount. רבא drank a lot, which is why it made him hungry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both facts can be true. רבא's practice involved a large quantity, which opens the appetite. A small amount still satisfies, so the distinction from oil remains.

phrases.english: A lot stimulates (the appetite),
a little satisfies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by distinguishing between quantities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine always whets the appetite, as with רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a large amount whets the appetite. A small amount satisfies.

steps.title: Challenge from a פסוק: only bread satisfies
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says wine gladdens and bread satisfies. That implies wine does not satisfy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does wine satisfy at all? It is written: 'Wine gladdens man's heart... and bread satisfies man's heart.' So bread is what satisfies, and wine does not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again, this time from a פסוק in תהלים. The פסוק seems to give 'satisfying' only to bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק assigns a different role to each item: wine brings joy, and bread satisfies. Reading it as a contrast suggests wine does not satisfy at all, which would knock out the distinction from step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (introduces a פסוק as a challenge)

phrases.english: And does it satisfy at all?!
But it is written: 'And wine gladdens the heart of man
and bread satisfies the heart of man, etc.'
Bread is what satisfies,
wine does not satisfy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A stronger challenge: wine may not satisfy even in small amounts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק contrasts wine (gladdens) with bread (satisfies). That implies wine does not satisfy.

steps.title: Wine has two qualities: it satisfies and gladdens
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק does not deny that wine satisfies. Wine both satisfies and gladdens, while bread only satisfies. The פסוק mentions joy for wine because that is its extra quality.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wine has two qualities: it satisfies and it gladdens. Bread satisfies, but it does not gladden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק is not a contrast. Wine has both qualities, and the פסוק highlights what is special about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses joy for wine because bread lacks joy, not because wine lacks satisfaction. So wine still satisfies, and this keeps the distinction from oil in place.

phrases.english: Rather, wine has two (qualities) in it:
it satisfies and gladdens.
Bread, as for satisfying, it satisfies;
as for gladdening, it does not gladden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinterprets the פסוק quoted in step 30.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק contrasts wine and bread, giving 'satisfying' only to bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine has both qualities. The פסוק names joy for wine because that is the quality bread lacks.

steps.title: If wine is so good, it should get ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: If wine satisfies just like bread, then after drinking it we should say the full three ברכות of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should say the three ברכות (of ברכת המזון) over it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the conclusion further. If wine satisfies like bread, why not treat it like bread for the ברכה afterward?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread gets the three-ברכה ברכת המזון because it satisfies. Wine now has that quality too, plus joy. So it seems wine should get the same after-ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The three ברכות of ברכת המזון

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי נְבָרֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת!
phrases.english: If so, let us recite three blessings over it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי נְבָרֵיךְ עֲלֵיהּ שָׁלֹשׁ בְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a troubling consequence from the conclusion of step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that wine satisfies like bread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If wine shares bread's satisfying quality, it should also share bread's after-ברכה.

steps.title: People do not make a meal out of wine
steps.stepSummary: ברכת המזון is for a food people make into a meal. People do not build their meals on wine, so wine does not get the three ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: People do not make their meals around it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ברכת המזון depends on being the base of a meal. Wine is never used that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Satisfying is enough to earn wine its own ברכה before drinking (בורא פרי הגפן). ברכת המזון needs more than that: it needs a food people actually set a meal on (קביעות סעודה). Wine does not meet that standard.

phrases.english: People do not establish their meals on it.

steps.whatToRemember: Wine gets its own ברכה (בורא פרי הגפן) and oil does not, because wine satisfies (סעיד) and gladdens. Still, wine does not get ברכת המזון, because people do not base a meal on it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ברכת המזון is tied to the idea of a set meal (קביעות סעודה), not only to how filling a food is.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 and closes the discussion of wine versus oil.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any food that satisfies like bread should get ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzMaskana: ברכת המזון also requires that people base meals on the food, and wine is not used that way.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wine's satisfying and gladdening qualities earn it a special ברכה before drinking, but not ברכת המזון afterward.

steps.title: What if someone makes wine his whole meal?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא about a person who actually builds his meal on wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: If someone did make his meal out of wine, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 33 said people don't build meals on wine. Now רב נחמן בר יצחק asks about a person who does build his meal on wine. Does he say the full ברכת המזון?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 33 depended on what people normally do. So the question is about one person who goes against the norm. Does his personal habit change the ברכה for him?

keyTerms.meaning: To set or establish a meal, to make something the base of a meal

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
If he established his meal on it (wine), what is the law?
phrases.notes: Should he then say the three ברכות of ברכת המזון?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of step 33 on an unusual individual.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does one person's choice to make wine his meal require ברכת המזון for him?

steps.title: Wait for אליהו; for now, one person's habit doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: רבא says only אליהו could tell us if wine can be a real meal. For now, one person's unusual intention is cancelled by what everyone else does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When אליהו comes and tells us whether wine can be a basis for a meal, we will know. But for now, at any rate, this person's intention is cancelled, because everyone else does not do this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers that the question can't be fully settled now. In practice, the person does not say the full ברכת המזון on wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכות follow what people normally do, not one person's private habit. Since almost nobody makes wine a meal, this person's plan is 'בטלה דעתו', meaning it is ignored. Only a prophet like אליהו could tell us otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: When אליהו comes (a question we cannot settle now)
Being a fixed basis for a meal
His intention is cancelled by the practice of all other people

steps.whatToRemember: In ברכות, one person's unusual habit is cancelled by what everyone else does (בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם). So wine never gets the full ברכת המזון.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule בטלה דעתו אצל כל אדם shows up all across ש״ס. A person's odd personal use usually does not change the halachic category of a food or object.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him:
When Eliyahu comes and says
whether it counts as a basis for a meal.
Now, at any rate,
his intention is cancelled relative to all other people.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְשֶׁיָּבֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ וְיֹאמַר אִי הָוֵי קְבִיעוּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34 and closes the wine discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Whether wine can be a meal is left for אליהו. In practice, the individual's intention is ignored and he does not say the three ברכות.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Wine does not get ברכת המזון, even for someone who makes it his meal.

steps.title: Back to the main statement: olive oil gets בורא פרי העץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the earlier statement that we say בורא פרי העץ on olive oil, quoted in the names of שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל, and רבי יצחק also said in the name of רבי יוחנן: On olive oil we say the ברכה 'בורא פרי העץ'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings back a statement that was quoted earlier in passing, so it can now look at it closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גופא means 'now let's study that statement itself.' The rule is that olive oil keeps the ברכה of its fruit, the olive. The next steps will ask what kind of case this could be.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself' — returning to examine a statement quoted earlier
The ברכה on fruit of the tree
And so too said (a second chain of rabbis with the same statement)

phrases.english: The matter itself.
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: and so too Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Olive oil — we make a blessing on it
'Who creates the fruit of the tree.'

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wine discussion and goes back to examine the olive oil statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on olive oil is בורא פרי העץ.

steps.title: How would someone drink oil? Plain oil is harmful
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case is. Drinking plain oil can't be the case, because it harms the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he drinks the oil plain, that harms him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what situation the rule is talking about. Then it rejects the first idea, drinking oil plain, because that is harmful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not make a ברכה on something that hurts us. So the rule cannot be about someone drinking oil by itself. The גמרא now needs to find another case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he drinks it as a plain drink —
it harms him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּקָא שָׁתֵי לֵיהּ מִשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to find the case for the rule in step 36 and rejects the first option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the rule is about drinking plain oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plain oil harms the drinker. Something harmful gets no ברכה.

steps.title: Proof from תרומה: drinking oil is harm, not benefit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says someone who drinks תרומה oil does not pay the extra fifth, but someone who rubs it on his body does. This shows drinking oil gives no benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Someone who (by mistake) drinks oil of תרומה pays back the value, but does not pay the extra fifth. Someone who rubs oil of תרומה on his body pays back the value and also pays the extra fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that drinking plain oil is harmful. The proof comes from the laws of eating תרומה by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra fifth (חומש) is paid only when the person got benefit from the תרומה. The one who rubs oil on himself pays it, because he benefited. The one who drank it does not pay it, which means drinking oil counts as damage, not benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to the כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
The extra fifth paid by someone who ate תרומה by mistake
Rubs or anoints (oil on the body)

steps.confusionAlert: The drinker pays less because he got no benefit from the oil. It is not that his act was less wrong. The extra fifth depends on benefit.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
One who drinks oil of תרומה —
pays the principal,
and does not pay the fifth.
One who anoints himself with oil of תרומה —

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וּמְשַׁלֵּם אֶת הַחוֹמֶשׁ.
phrases.english: pays the principal and pays the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 37 that drinking oil is harmful.
steps.raayaObject: That drinking plain oil harms a person and gives no benefit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the drinker of תרומה oil pays no חומש, while one who anoints with it does.

steps.title: Maybe he eats the oil with bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is someone eating oil by dipping bread into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is that he eats the oil together with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: Since plain oil doesn't work, the גמרא tries a new case: oil eaten with bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil with bread is a normal, healthy way to have oil. So this case avoids the harm problem from step 37. The next step will test it.

keyTerms.meaning: By means of bread, together with bread

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּקָא אָכֵיל לֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי פַּת.
phrases.english: Rather, it is where he eats it by means of bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָא אָכֵיל לֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי פַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new case after step 37 rejected plain drinking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is drinking plain oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is eating oil with bread (to be tested next).

steps.title: With bread, the bread is main and covers the oil
steps.stepSummary: If the oil is eaten with bread, the bread is the main food and the oil is secondary. A משנה says the ברכה on the main food covers the secondary food.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the bread is the main food and the oil is secondary. And we learned in a משנה: This is the rule — whenever there is a main food and a secondary food with it, one makes the ברכה on the main food, and that covers the secondary food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the bread case. With bread, the oil would get no ברכה of its own at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of עיקר וטפל says the main food's ברכה covers the side food. When bread is dipped in oil, the bread is the main food. So the ברכה would be המוציא, not בורא פרי העץ on the oil.

keyTerms.meaning: The secondary food, eaten only to go with the main food

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of עיקר וטפל is a basic rule of ברכות used every day. For example, a side food eaten to help the main food is covered by the main food's ברכה.

phrases.english: If so,

phrases.aramaic: הָוְיָא לֵיהּ פַּת עִיקָּר וְהוּא טָפֵל.
phrases.english: the bread is the main food and it (the oil) is secondary.
And we learned in a משנה: This is the rule:
Anything that is main and has a secondary food with it —

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הָעִיקָּר וּפוֹטֵר אֶת הַטְּפֵלָה!
phrases.english: one blesses on the main food and exempts the secondary food!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הָוְיָא לֵיהּ פַּת עִיקָּר וְהוּא טָפֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the bread case suggested in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the case is oil eaten with bread.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With bread, the oil is secondary and covered by the bread's ברכה, so it would never get בורא פרי העץ.

steps.title: The case is oil drunk mixed into אניגרון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new case: the person drinks the oil mixed into a drink called אניגרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is that he drinks the oil by means of 'אניגרון'.
steps.whatsHappening: After two cases were rejected, the גמרא offers a third: oil drunk inside a vegetable-water drink called אניגרון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mixed into this drink, the oil is no longer harmful, so the first problem is gone. On the next amud, the גמרא raises the same main-and-secondary problem for אניגרון and resolves it. Next it defines the word אניגרון.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink made from cooked vegetable water mixed with oil

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּקָא שָׁתֵי לֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי ״אֲנִיגְרוֹן״,
phrases.english: Rather, it is where he drinks it by means of 'anigeron',

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּקָא שָׁתֵי לֵיהּ עַל יְדֵי אֲנִיגְרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a third case after step 40 rejected the bread case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case is oil eaten with bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is oil drunk mixed into אניגרון.

steps.title: רבה בר שמואל defines אניגרון and אנסיגרון
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל explains that אניגרון is water from cooked beets, and starts to define אנסיגרון. The definition continues into the next passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה בר שמואל said: 'אניגרון' is the water of cooked beets; 'אנסיגרון' is the water (of... — continued in the next section).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the strange word אניגרון means. It also starts defining a similar word, אנסיגרון. This sentence is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step adds a definition, not a new argument. Knowing that אניגרון is beet water helps us picture the case: oil mixed into a vegetable broth.

keyTerms.meaning: Water of beets (water in which beets were cooked)
A similar drink with a different base (defined in the next section)

phrases.english: As Rabba bar Shmuel said:
'Anigeron' is water of beets,
'Ansigeron' is the water
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֲנִיגְרוֹן מַיָּא דְסִלְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the term אניגרון used in step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אניגרון is water in which beets were cooked. The definition of אנסיגרון begins and continues on the next amud.
